body:
Walkthrough

The host reads one request from stdin and writes a response to stdout. It lists installed PWAs, matches requests to installed apps, detects browser context, and starts Chrome with selected directories and app or URL arguments. **Changes: PWA host flow** |Layer / File(s)|Summary| |:---|:---| |**PWA metadata discovery**
`host/pwa.go`|The host derives app IDs, display modes, and domains from browser Preferences, Sync LevelDB files, and History files.| |**Installed PWA catalogue and matching**
`host/pwa.go`|The host combines launcher URLs with recovered metadata to list installed PWAs. It matches target hosts to app domains.| |**Request handling and Chrome launch**
`host/main.go`, `host/pwa.go`|The host handles list and launch requests, selects an installed app and browser context, resolves a Chrome binary, starts the process, and returns the result.| **Estimated code review effort:** 4 (Complex) | ~45 minutes **Change:** Feature
Merge Risk: Moderate · up to c31d8

The host can open the wrong browser or profile for an installed PWA, and it can hide apps that are able to open in a window. These are real functional gaps in a new native host. This PR is labelled as an experiment that must not be merged, and no tests are included.

**Explanation** The title says this is a review-only experiment labelled e2c-label-by-app and marked do not merge. The changeset adds a Go host (host/main.go) and Linux Chrome-family PWA discovery (host/pwa.go) that launch installed PWAs by app ID or URL. The title names no part of that functionality. It describes the PR's status, not its change, so it is off-topic and misleading as a title for the code. **Resolution** Rename the PR to describe the main change, for example: "Add Linux PWA discovery and launch host". Keep the experiment label out of the title, or move it to the description. If this PR is only an experiment that will not merge, state that in the description and close it as the objectives describe.

Inline comments: Review comments at @host/main.go: - Line 133: After app lookup in the launch flow, return an error when the app is unavailable and both appID and req.URL are empty, rather than starting Chrome without a launch target. Preserve the existing URL fallback whenever req.URL is available. - Line 170: Update PWAInfo and the launch flow around findChromeBinary so the selected app launches with the executable of the browser that owns its matched launcher. Preserve the existing user-data and profile settings; alternatively, restrict listInstalledPWAs to launchers owned by the browser used for launch. Review comments at @host/pwa.go: - Around line 23-24: Update the argument parsing used by userDataRegex and profileRegex to handle desktop Exec quoting before extracting directory switches, and parse /proc command lines by splitting on NUL while preserving spaces within each argument. Apply the same behaviour to both directory options so values such as “Profile 1” are passed to Chrome intact. - Line 111: App-ID candidates built with u.Hostname() drop non-default ports and fail to match port-specific manifest IDs; update all three URL reconstructions in the surrounding app-ID matching flow to use u.Host while preserving the existing scheme and path behavior. - Line 145: Update the appModes lookup so display settings are keyed by user-data directory, profile, and app ID rather than app ID alone. Resolve each launcher using its matching installation’s setting, and ensure catalogue filtering preserves installations whose own display mode enables a window. - Around line 241-243: Update the LevelDB scan that builds appModes from allDBFiles so it selects each app’s current display_mode using LevelDB record ordering, including sequence numbers and deletion markers, rather than file or scan order; use a reader that exposes the required ordering and tombstone information, and preserve the catalogue’s existing handling of the resulting mode. - Around line 132-135: Update extractDisplayMode to parse the protobuf wire format and read field 3 only at the top level, skipping length-delimited nested messages such as icon_infos; treat an absent user_display_mode_default as no explicit setting.
